faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: Cold Mind is a detective game. A client gives you live remote access to one phone belonging to someone at the centre of their case — sometimes a victim, sometimes a suspect, sometimes a missing person, sometimes the client themselves. You are reading it as it is right now. Everything you need to solve the case is somewhere on it.
faq.a2: Open the questions from the round button at the bottom of the phone's home screen, dig through its apps for clues, and answer. Solve a question to unlock the next one.
faq.a3: Most questions are free text — the checker looks for the key fact, a name, place, date or amount, not your exact wording. Others ask you to put events in order, pick someone out of a line-up, tap the statement that does not hold up, or select every item that proves something. Answers are graded on your device; nothing you type is sent anywhere.
faq.q4: An app is locked. How do I open it?
faq.a4: Apps unlock as you progress. Look for passwords, login codes or notes hidden inside other apps — emails and chats usually point the way.
faq.a5: Re-read the conversations, emails, photos and payment history of the people involved — most answers hide in the small details. Each question also names the app its answer is in, and the board shows you who everyone is. If you get the same question wrong three times we can offer you a hand; you can turn that offer on or off under Answer hints in Settings.
faq.a6: Tap the folder button at the bottom of the phone's home screen to go back to the case list, then scroll to the case you want.
faq.a7: Yes — your solved questions and current case are saved automatically on your device.
faq.a8: Pro unlocks every case, and every case added later. You can subscribe from the GET PRO button — it is on the case list, on the phone's top row, and at the top of Settings.
faq.a9: A corkboard of everyone and everywhere the case touches, opened with the pin button at the bottom of the phone's home screen. Tap anything pinned to it to see the photograph properly and read the whole of what is written under it. It is the case as it looks before you start — it will not give you the answer.
faq.q10: I changed the language but the cases are still in English.
faq.a10: That is expected for now. The menus, buttons and help are translated into every language we ship, but the cases themselves — the messages, emails and notes on the phone — are currently written only in English. Translating them is work we still owe you.
faq.empty: Frequently asked questions are coming soon.
q.prompt_body:
If you get the same question wrong three times, we can show you two options to pick from — one right, one wrong.

You can change this anytime in Settings.
q.contradiction_single: Tap the statement that doesn't hold up:
q.multi_prompt: Select every statement the phone actually proves:
q.contradiction_pair: Tap the two statements that contradict each other:
q.wrong_generic: Not quite. Keep investigating and try again.
q.hint_wrong: That's not the right one — try the other option.
q.all_done: You have answered every question in this case.
q.locked_body: You've cracked the first clues. Unlock Premium to keep answering and solve the rest of the case.
board.title: The Board
q.timeline_prompt: Drag the events into the right order — earliest at the top:
solved.title: Case Solved
solved.body: You uncovered the truth in {{client}}'s case. Every question answered correctly.
solved.replay_confirm_body: Every answer, every app you signed into and the ending you chose will be wiped, and the case goes back to question one. This cannot be undone.
eval.wrong: Not quite. Re-check the evidence and try again.
eval.timeline_no: The order isn't right yet. Re-check the timestamps.
eval.suspect_ok: Correct — the evidence points squarely at them.
eval.suspect_no: The evidence doesn't convict them. Look again at who had means and motive.
eval.multi_extra: Too many — one of those doesn't actually prove it.
eval.multi_missing: You're missing a piece of the proof.
eval.multi_wrong: Not the right set — re-check which items actually prove it.
eval.contra_ok: Correct — that statement breaks the story.
eval.contra_no: That holds up. Find the line that contradicts the rest.
